cases.title: Call disconnects immediately on answer
cases.diagnosis: The old read path could return NULL after a partial frame or transient SCO failure. NULL means channel termination, not temporarily missing audio. The iPhone also replaced SCO around answer.
cases.resolution: Keep call lifecycle separate from audio socket lifecycle; return ast_null_frame, discard incomplete buffers on disconnect and accept the replacement socket.
cases.validation_and_limits: A real 20.6.0 call survived SCO replacement with the local correction. With a nonblocking socket pair and a model smoother, the stock callback from 20.22.0, 22.12.0, 24.0.0 and master cfb0aa2a returned NULL after 48 bytes and EAGAIN. The corrected regression test covers EOF, reset and reconnect.

cases.title: One-way audio despite successful Bluetooth writes
cases.diagnosis: An intermediate agent change confused on-air eSCO packet length with host PCM framing. The tested device used 60-byte radio values and 48-byte host blocks; socket MTU is a limit.
cases.resolution: Observe valid received 16-bit PCM block length, bounded by SCO_OPTIONS; reset partial buffers when size or socket changes. Do not hard-code 48 or 60.
cases.validation_and_limits: The test covers 48/60/96/120-byte host blocks and socket MTU bounds. Hardware showed 48-byte host PCM and a 60-byte radio length. RX/TX framing on other transports still requires measurement.

cases.title: RTP arrives but outgoing Bluetooth audio stops intermittently
cases.diagnosis: The distribution translator patch retained old sequence history across a new SSRC. A smaller random new sequence looked late; RTP kept arriving but no PCM reached mbl_write.
cases.resolution: Opt-in RtpSourceReset framehook resets translator sequence history on AST_CONTROL_SRCCHANGE. Keep late packet rejection for the same source. Inspect the installed distro code, not only upstream version tags.
cases.validation_and_limits: A separate unprivileged Noble 20.6.0 instance yielded 250/450 valid PCMA-to-PCM frames, with complete loss in four of nine phases. With the local workaround, 450/450 frames were valid and an extra late packet produced no additional PCM. The package patch is tracked by Debian and Ubuntu. Rebuild the workaround against the target ABI.

cases.title: iPhone Bluetooth Show Notifications switch is missing
keywords: iOS iPhone 16 MAP OBEX MessageAccess permission access denied missing toggle
cases.diagnosis: Working HFP pairing did not expose MAP permission initially. The first MAP request returned access denied. After reopening the Bluetooth device details the switch appeared.
cases.resolution: Pair/connect; issue one MAP access request; reopen Settings → Bluetooth → device info; enable Show Notifications. Then retry reading. Do not repeatedly re-pair as the first response.
cases.validation_and_limits: Observed on one iPhone 16, with the original iOS build unrecorded. Enabling Show Notifications allowed reading. Outgoing PushMessage was tested separately. Apple acknowledged the private product feedback without a public case number.

cases.title: Previously delivered SMS appears again after reconnect
keywords: MAP timestamp shifted one second duplicate SMS message handle fingerprint
cases.diagnosis: The iPhone re-reported one message with a timestamp one second earlier. A metadata-based identity treated it as new.
cases.resolution: Store sender/body digest and tolerate ±2 seconds; retain aliases for changed metadata keys. Do not resend old rows during migration.
cases.validation_and_limits: The same message returned with a timestamp one second earlier. The local tolerance is two seconds, so two genuine identical messages from one sender in that window may coalesce. The iPhone observation was included in Apple Product Feedback.

cases.title: PushMessage completes but recipient has no SMS
keywords: iPhone MAP Uploading bMessage originator vCard green bubble Not Delivered SMS iMessage
cases.diagnosis: MAP completion means phone acceptance, not carrier delivery. One accepted transfer produced Not Delivered; manual SMS retry succeeded. A later new message arrived automatically after delay.
cases.resolution: Use UTF-8 bMessage with originator/recipient structure; distinguish queued, submitting, handed-to-phone and unknown. Never automatically repeat an ambiguous cellular send.
cases.validation_and_limits: One accepted upload was followed by a delivery failure on the phone. A later new message arrived automatically. The originator vCard and phone send mode both changed. Long multipart messages and carrier receipts remain unverified. BlueZ #2897 requests an API documentation cross-reference.

cases.title: SMS goes to a different number from the contact card
keywords: Linphone iOS address book multiple numbers SIP MESSAGE sms- prefix
cases.diagnosis: User observed Linphone selecting another number from a multi-number contact. Separate malformed @ input also occurred. No upstream client code defect was independently proven.
cases.resolution: Use sms-972501234567@home.example.net on the authenticated Home SIM account, select that exact SIP result. Strip sms- server-side before number normalization.
cases.validation_and_limits: The prefix workaround worked on the observed iOS 6.2.2 client. Source inspection on 6.2.2 and 6.2.4 found recipient rows omitting an address and a SIPS display formatting issue. The exact taps leading to the wrong number were not recorded.

cases.title: invalid-address even when MESSAGE(to) is correct
keywords: Asterisk AGI BASE64_ENCODE truncated .org .o UTF-8 exact LEN multiline
cases.diagnosis: The original MESSAGE(to) was complete, but the tested BASE64_ENCODE/AGI path lost trailing bytes at some lengths. Short check addresses masked the problem.
cases.resolution: Read exact raw byte length reported by LEN; validate delimiters and UTF-8. Keep message text out of argv/logs. Do not attribute this to the Base64 algorithm itself.
cases.validation_and_limits: The upstream buffer allocation defect is tracked in Asterisk #940 and fixed by #941. Tag 20.6.0 has the old sizing formula, and 20.11.0 has the correction. The separate gateway workaround was checked for byte equality of the full URI, multiline Unicode body, Call-ID and CSeq over authenticated TLS.

cases.title: Registered client immediately receives 488 or cannot establish media
keywords: Linphone third-party account RTP/SAVP RTP/SAVPF use_avpf SRTP SDES TLS
cases.diagnosis: The new third-party account offered SAVP while its endpoint expected SAVPF. A different route of the same client offered a different profile.
cases.resolution: Match SDP per endpoint; for the observed third-party account use_avpf=no, keep mandatory SDES SRTP and TLS. Do not disable encryption to hide profile mismatch.
cases.validation_and_limits: Authenticated echo and real calls passed. Do not copy one endpoint profile to all Linphone routes.

cases.title: Caller number exists in SIP but is not displayed
keywords: iPhone Bluetooth CNAM eight spaces display name CALLERID num Linphone
cases.diagnosis: From URI contained the number but Bluetooth CNAM supplied eight spaces as display name.
cases.resolution: Set caller ID display name from number before Dial, preserving privacy policy.
cases.validation_and_limits: User confirmed number on external incoming call; empty display data is not evidence of missing signaling.

cases.title: Call connects with missing audio or does not hang up
keywords: Sagemcom port forwarding range InternalPort collapse hairpin NAT Contact ACK BYE local_net
cases.diagnosis: The tested router API range rule mapped multiple external RTP ports to one internal port. Separately, broad local_net classification on hairpin calls advertised a private Contact.
cases.resolution: Use verified per-port forwarding and narrow transport local_net appropriate to topology. Check Contact/SDP, ACK and BYE in both LAN hairpin and truly external calls.
cases.validation_and_limits: Sagemcom F@ST 5670 HW 2.00, firmware SGFx10000381. Hairpin UDP probes to external 10000, 10002 and 10198 were delivered to internal 10000. Sixteen individual mappings preserved their ports. Return traffic was verified on 10000, 10006 and 10014. Direct WAN behavior of the original range rule was not isolated.

cases.title: Public name points to unavailable IPv6
keywords: DuckDNS AAAA IPv6 prefix delegation absent stale global address IPv4
cases.diagnosis: ISP prefix availability varied; stale AAAA could point to an address no longer assigned.
cases.resolution: Update A/AAAA from the intended host and explicitly clear obsolete AAAA when no valid global IPv6 exists. Distinguish address absence from observation failure.
cases.validation_and_limits: Working voice acceptance used IPv4. Returning IPv6 requires separate SIP/RTP/firewall verification.

cases.title: Russian SIP MESSAGE is mojibake despite Russian menus
keywords: T780P CP1251 CP1252 UTF-8 glyph chart bytes 0-255 transliteration Hebrew
cases.diagnosis: Localized menu fonts did not imply Unicode support for received messages. Actual glyphs differed from assumed encoding tables.
cases.resolution: Use empirical byte charts and the recorded visual-russian-v2 mapping for this firmware. Control bytes yielded no useful extra alphabet; NUL truncated display.
cases.validation_and_limits: On firmware V78.5.3.1 SVN13200 and hardware 18.01.01.0, incoming direct UTF-8 with an explicit charset still displayed incorrectly. ASCII was readable and the phone sent UTF-8 from its own web UI. These observations were sent privately to LVswitch service.

cases.title: SIP URI pasted into search fails or uses unexpected transport
keywords: Linphone iOS search field sip sips leading colon transport=tls 5061
cases.diagnosis: The client log showed unexpected UDP in one attempt and a malformed leading colon in another. Origin of the extra character was not established.
cases.resolution: Clear search completely; in the observed UI enter user@home.example.net:5061;transport=tls without sip: and select the exact result. Full SIP URI syntax in other APIs remains valid.
cases.validation_and_limits: Verified on the tested client workflow. Do not generalize to every Linphone version or claim SIPS is inherently broken.

cases.title: Seven service messages appear at once after one SMS
keywords: Linphone push notification batching queued check status spam
cases.diagnosis: Server recorded four checks, one old rejection and two success-path statuses at different times. User saw seven together. One cellular request existed; batching location was not identified.
cases.resolution: Do not send diagnostic or queued notifications to the user chat. Keep one phone-acceptance notice and explicit errors. Record diagnostic results in logs.
cases.validation_and_limits: Do not claim seven SMS sends, or blame a particular client/server queue without evidence. A quiet check verified no new chat message.

cases.title: Outbound SIP MESSAGE loses its explicit charset
cases.diagnosis: The parsed Content-Type header includes media parameters, but update_content_type() copies only media type and subtype into the outgoing body.
cases.resolution: Preserve parsed media parameters when constructing the outgoing message. A separate direct encoding test can isolate a legacy handset renderer.
cases.validation_and_limits: Ubuntu Noble 20.6.0 sent text/plain for text/plain with charset=UTF-8. The independent X-Probe-Type header retained the full value. The application/json control and both message bodies arrived intact. The same function was inspected in 22.12.0, 24.0.0 and master cfb0aa2a.

cases.title: Bluetooth SCO listener wakes about 1,000 times per second at idle
cases.diagnosis: The listener polls the SCO accept context without waiting, then waits one millisecond on the empty audio I/O context.
cases.resolution: Wait for socket readiness on the accept context with a one-second upper bound for unload.
cases.validation_and_limits: On the tested 20.6.0 package the idle thread went from 981.34 to 1.00 voluntary context switches per second. Eight standalone scenarios passed in optimized and sanitizer builds. The patch applies without fuzz to three later releases and master.

cases.title: IAX2 schedules 50 timer wakeups per second with no active trunks
cases.diagnosis: At the default 20 ms trunk frequency the periodic timer remains armed when there are no runtime trunk peers.
cases.resolution: Start the timer under the peer list lock when the first peer is created. Stop it when cleanup removes the last peer, and update the active rate on reload.
cases.validation_and_limits: On the tested 20.6.0 package the idle network thread went from 49.99 to 1.00 voluntary context switches per second. A Linux timerfd harness covered failures and 1,000 creation/cleanup races. Earlier protocol checks used two isolated instances of the actual module.

cases.title: Gateway panel stalls during first Home Assistant setup
cases.diagnosis: The gateway custom component stalled while importing its first Home Assistant config entry. Configuration validation had passed.
cases.resolution: Schedule the import in a Home Assistant task and return from domain setup. Perform the coordinator refresh and platform setup in the config-entry handler.
cases.validation_and_limits: The corrected installation exposed three dashboard tabs and 25 entities through the API. Nine isolated forwarding-policy tests passed. The route-status check and the live call tests cover different behaviors.
